parts_missing: 'red' rash: only Purpuric rash is used. Petechiae of skin (disorder) is not a descendant of Purpuric rash, so a petechial or red non-blanching rash will not match
elements.problem: Every part is encoded: temp >= 38 °C, Headache, Stiff neck and Purpuric rash, OR-ed under Seizure, giving probable Meningitis, which the Urgent rule references via active_condition. But the OR reading means Seizure + plain Headache (very common after a fit) or Seizure + fever alone produces a PROBABLE meningitis diagnosis. As a referral trigger that is acceptable; as a 'probable' diagnosis it is over-broad and clinically doubtful. It also makes the separate new/worse-headache criteria redundant. Consider requiring >= 2 items (any2) or downgrading to possible.

elements.problem: Common faint likely is encoded as probable Vasovagal syncope: Collapse AND Muscle twitch AND any of flushing/dizziness/nausea/sweating. The page lists the prodrome as 'flushing, dizziness, nausea, sweating', which is plausibly any one, so OR is acceptable. Without the brevity and rapid-recovery discriminators, the rule cannot tell a faint from a seizure: a real generalised seizure recorded as collapse + twitching with nausea or dizziness would be called a probable faint. There is no anchor or exclusion against a confirmed Seizure.

rule_level_problems.problem: The OR over fever/headache/stiff neck/rash means Seizure + Headache alone (common post-ictally) yields a PROBABLE meningitis diagnosis, and Seizure + any fever does too. The referral consequence matches the page, but the probable diagnosis is over-called. It also makes the 'new/worse headache' criteria and part of the diagnostic picture redundant.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: same-day referral after a seizure/fit
rule_level_problems.problem: Three time clauses depend on recorded-onset semantics: decreased consciousness > 1 h after fit, BP >= 180/130 > 1 h after fit, and postpartum <= 1 week. The first two are anchored to the Seizure record's onset (usually 'now' at triage), so they will rarely fire when the referral decision is made. The postpartum bound is anchored to the record time, not delivery, so it does not restrict anything.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable stroke / Diagnose probable TIA (seizure/fit page)
rule_level_problems.problem: No due_to anchor or context, and Difficulty talking / Visual disturbance carry no New/Sudden qualifier. Any adult with a recorded visual disturbance or speech difficulty gets probable stroke AND probable TIA.

The discriminators that separate a faint from a seizure (twitching < 15 s, rapid recovery) are missing, and the rule does not exclude a confirmed Seizure. A seizure presenting as collapse + twitching + nausea can be called a probable vasovagal syncope at the same time as the Urgent seizure referral.

rule_level_problems.problem: The check_for, triggered by Seizure, includes the 'No (not a seizure)' branch findings (Collapse, Muscle twitch, Flushing, etc.). That is coherent only if the faint rule is meant to compete with the seizure label. The page's Yes/No confirmation step is not modelled.

summary: Most red-box criteria are present with correct concepts and thresholds. The biggest problem is that the meningitis 'probable' rule fires on Seizure plus any single item, including plain headache. Next come the onset-based timing clauses (decreased consciousness or BP > 1 h after the fit, postpartum <= 1 week), which are anchored to record time and so misfire or never restrict. The stroke/TIA and common-faint rules lose their discriminators (new/sudden on speech/vision; < 15 s twitching and rapid recovery) and have no context anchor, while 'unable to measure' glucose, the malaria/6-hour branch and 'consider epilepsy' are missing.
